topics.topic: How placement and publication affect observations sharing the same source_id
questions: When two different names have the same content and therefore the same source_id, does a placement or publication apply to every observation with that source_id, or only to the name used by the delivery action?

When several current file names have the same `source_id`, does a placement or publication for that source make every such observation `placed` or `published`, or only the observation whose name was used for delivery?

When several file names have the same source_id and one of them is delivered or published, do all of their observations become placed or published with the same references, or only the observation for the file name that was chosen?

A scan covers the photo folder and all its subfolders (R0-12). When a subfolder that is not ignored
cannot be listed, the whole operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`, so a partial scan is
never reported as complete. A file exactly at the source limit passes that rule. A file that
disappears before its metadata is read is not reported. Files with the same content are each reported,
with the same source id.
1. A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).
judgement.why: State 2 makes placement and publication status content-based, so every reported file with that content receives the status of the shared project-and-content placement and mark.

topics.topic: Ownership and timing of delivery, PhotoPlacement, publication, and PlacementOutcome creation
questions: Does “delivery” mean the deliverer's primitive `deliver one photo` operation, or the calling flow's whole place-publish-record sequence, and exactly who creates PlacementOutcome from which facts?

How can a PhotoPlacement be created and returned before the separate Portal publication and publication-recording actions if its non-optional `publication` already exists, and is recording publication a mutation of the placement despite M04 saying it is never rewritten?

quotes:
The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its
publication. When to scan, what to deliver next, what to repeat and which failure to treat as temporary
belong to the calling flow.

A delivery starts from an action of the owner in the workplace. The workplace lists the photos
that are ready, the owner chooses what to deliver, and the calling flow places, publishes and
marks each chosen photo in that order. The owner sees the result of each photo: delivered, or
failed with its reason. A failed photo does not stop the others. The service delivers nothing by
itself.

The answer to one delivery. It holds the placement facts when there is a placement, and the Portal
`photo_id` when the photo is already marked as published.

The record that one source photo of one project was placed in the Portal binary store. The
deliverer creates it once when placing a photo. A repeated placement returns it and writes nothing
(P-06). `name` is the source's relative path when it was placed and is not updated later. `sha256`,
`size` and `media_type` describe the stored image, while `source_id` is the hash of the source.

The body the calling flow sends to the Portal's `photo.publish`. `intake_id` identifies the
delivery of one source photo to one project: the deliverer derives it from the placement identity
as `deliverer-photo-<project_id>-<source_id>`, so a repeated publication is
recognised by the Portal. `intake_source` states where the photo entered the system and is always
`syncthing`. `client_visible` is always false (R0-06). The deliverer builds the body once within
M04.

The calling flow records the Portal photo id at the deliverer right after publishing. The
Portal is not changed for this. The experiment found that the Portal's photo list does not
return `intake_id`, and that publishing a photo again after it was shown answers 409.
judgement.why: Delivery is the deliverer's one-photo primitive that creates the outcome and placement before the calling flow publishes and records a mark; PhotoPlacement.publication is the immutable Portal publication body, not the later publication mark.

topics.topic: Whether ignored names appear as SourcePhotoObservation scan results
questions: Are temporary, hidden, `.trashed-`, and Syncthing conflict-copy entries absent from the scan result, or represented by SourcePhotoObservation, and if represented, which available status and reason describe them?

Does a scan create a SourcePhotoObservation for temporary files, hidden names and Syncthing conflict copies, or are those files absent from the scan result despite the product statement that the result contains each file?

quotes:
A name is ignored at every level of the path when, after the letters A to Z are lowered and no other
character is changed, it begins with an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_PREFIXES` constant, ends with
an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_SUFFIXES` constant, or contains the imported `CONFLICT_COPY_MARK`
constant, the mark of a Syncthing conflict copy (R0-14). Names beginning with a dot include Syncthing's
`.syncthing.*`, `.stfolder` and `.stversions` and the phone's `.trashed-*` files. A file Syncthing is still
writing lies under such a temporary name. Ignored names are not reported, ignored folders are not entered,
and an entry the listing shows as a symbolic link is neither reported nor followed.
- INV-18: a scan never reports a Syncthing conflict copy.
judgement.why: State 2 explicitly says ignored temporary, hidden, trashed, and conflict-copy names are absent from scan results rather than represented by SourcePhotoObservation.
